title: Equality cases in the sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb–Thirring inequality
coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX: the introduction, preliminaries, action, spectral-bound, compactness and rigidity sections, and both appendices. I checked the following by hand.
(1) Trace-deficit theorem. The Riccati identities V+t=S^2+i[B,S]=T^2-i[B,T]; the L/Z decomposition; tr(R(V+t))=trL-tr(RZ^2); the log-determinant evaluation F=trV/sqrt t-2tr(L-sqrt t); F>=0; tr(PV)=F+G+tr(RZ^2); tF'=-F/2-G, hence the integral of t^beta G equals sigma times the integral of t^beta F; the noncommutative square expansion; and the choice D=N^r giving trN^q/q.
(2) Field and path appendix. The formula for f_delta'; mu_delta(z)=(z+delta)^sigma-delta^sigma; the directional Jensen bound; N=M+delta^sigma; the endpoint integral for J_delta. In the path proposition: the CC^T identity, the Cholesky orbit at theta=0 and its derivative isomorphism, freeness of the sign action, the mod-2 count of orbits, and removal of the cutoff.
(3) Action identity and the penalty limit. I also checked that c_* does not depend on the dimension: the bounds on R(t) for t in [1,2], the commutator and V-N^r estimates, and the algebra relating F to Delta that gives E_{n,delta}.
(4) Compactness. The triangular gap T_j; boundedness of each row's coefficients; the tail bound from rank at most m via Jensen with r>1; the HS limit of A_j and the x-dependent operator-norm limit of B_j.
(5) Rigidity. Constant kernels via Gronwall; constant ranges via P'=0; B_0'=r(B_0^2-alpha^2); the tanh Riccati solution and the profile q(alpha^2-b^2)=(r+1)alpha^2 sech^2; the reduction of the complex case through the commuting projection.
(6) Attainment. The factorisations Q*Q=H+a^2 and QQ*>=a^2 (this uses r>1); the kernel sech^{1/r}; the integral of V^p; and agreement between C_gamma=D_sigma/b_sigma and the Gamma-function formula.
I found no gaps. The only nit is that the Sobolev constant 2 is not sharp, which is harmless.
main_claim: For 1/2<gamma<3/2, Tr(-d^2/dx^2-W)_-^gamma <= C_gamma ∫tr W^{gamma+1/2} for m×m Hermitian W>=0. Equality holds if and only if, in some constant unitary basis, W=diag((r+1)a_j^2 sech^2(r a_j(x-x_j)), 0,...) with at most m nonzero channels and r=(gamma-1/2)^{-1}.
sibling_notes: There were no prior entries in family 262. The paper re-proves the analytic foundations it takes from companion MLT (trace deficit, field, connecting path) in its appendices, so it does not depend on MLT's proofs.
